prospect.name: Omar

prospect.training_background: Lifelong athlete — played sports all his life including contact sports, still playing full basketball games and two football games a day in rec leagues until relatively recently. Currently holds a private gym membership where he does boxing training, mitt work and sparring, plus group classes. Has incorporated kettlebells occasionally but never consistently.
prospect.medical: Accumulated wear from contact sports — ankles, knees, shoulders, elbows and neck. Rates general pain 7 out of 10, worst on the first steps in the morning; one elbow reaches 8-9 on pushing and pulling movements and forces him to lower weight or skip exercises. Describes a compensation chain rated 10 for cumulative effect: 'whether it was my ankle at first, and now it's my knees, my right knee because I'm compensating, and now my hip, my lower back.' No diagnosed conditions disclosed; none were asked about. Age given only as 'over 40'; height and weight never stated.

notable.note: The best ICP fit in this batch and it did not close, which makes it the most useful call here. He matches the stated ICP on every criterion including the neglected-health line almost verbatim, and he explicitly said money was not the obstacle. What blocked him was proof and detail — he found Trevor the previous day, was asked for $6,000 by a self-identified salesman he had never met, and had to demand a breakdown of what he was buying. Two process issues. First, the rep quoted the price as a range, '$1,000 to $9,000', before discovery was finished and at the prospect's prompting, then had to explain that the cheap end is non-personalised programmes — which discloses a $1,000 option and invites anchoring downward; the prospect immediately probed 'where does the 1,000 fit?'. Second, the prospect's single named adoption blocker, no kettlebells available in the hotels and Latin American gyms he lives out of, got a genuinely poor answer: find a gym, most probably have them, and 'you're in sales, so you know how to do some problem solving'. The real answer, that Trevor also programmes calisthenics and maces, surfaced thirty minutes later by accident.
